unmapped_findings: The polycrystalline Fe-12%Al alloy (with 60 ppm C) showed only a weak effect of quenching, in contrast to the strong quench effect found for the Fe-16%Al alloy.
Real composition of the Fe-12%Al polycrystal (Table 1): 12.0 at.% (6.2 wt.-%) Al; impurity contents C 50-60 wt.ppm, Si 60-90 wt.ppm, Cu <40 wt.ppm.

In the quenched Fe-12%Al the deformation substructure consisted of glide bands with dislocation tangles between them, whereas the furnace-cooled alloy developed a dislocation cell structure; i.e. quenching before deformation also reduces dislocation mobility, which is attributed to the presence of quenched-in excess vacancies.
